title: Memory of Shadows
text:
Upon the white pillow,

beyond desire,

upon the white night,

upon the white silence,

upon ourselves,

the souls in their meeting.


Upon my raised forehead,

the exact moment,

you say that in a shadow

you live in my memory.


Synthesis of the hours.

You and I in motion,

fighting life to life,

delighting body to body.


You say that in these shadows

you live in my memory,

and they are the same shadows

that are living inside me.
editorial_note: The translation treats the source's likely typo as 'Synthesis' and keeps the poem's white silence and living shadows.

title: I Came
text:
I came with the desire to love people,

and they have gone on drying my generous root.

I see Life rowing among turbid lagoons.

Each thing, as it passes, leaves wakes of mud...


And I speak this way, I who have been victorious in my world,

because I was able to conquer myself and conquer desire.

But I have not wanted to deceive myself by inventing

an equivocal image. I forged myself in all I see...


I do not wake to an hour that does not bring with it,

in a deaf silence, a hooked complaint.

The soul has an ear that hears and feels it

and receives this complaint with doubled sorrow...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's generous root, muddy wakes, and soul-ear of complaint.

title: Wherever One Looks
text:
Wherever one looks,

nothing can be seen on earth,

for light is no longer light,

but black shadow without truce,

and along every road

blood reaches up to the chest.


Why this mingling of bloods,

some old and others new?

What do the gods

of the future need, that they mix them?


I think there is a reason,

and I hope to be able to know it.

Only a white hope

makes me live for it.

I still want to believe

that the bloods confronting one another

in this hard battle

of souls and veins

must give us a light

that must break the darkness.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the wartime darkness, mingled bloods, and stubborn white hope.

title: I Would Like to Have Several Spare Smiles
text:
I would like to have several spare smiles

and a vast repertory of ways to express myself.

Either with words, or with manners,

to seek the skillful gesture that might shield me...


And, as with the gesture, to seek in lying

different disguises, to dress deception well;

and to be able, without conscience, to go around giving people,

with subtle maneuvering, the caress of harm.


I would like to-and I cannot!-be as others are,

those who people the world and call themselves human:

always the kiss on the lip, hiding the facts,

and in the end... washing their hands so calmly.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the speaker's bitter wish for social masks she cannot wear.

title: One of Those Instants One Lives
text:
One of those instants one lives

not knowing in what world, or in what time,

when the soul is not felt and barely

the existence of our body is felt,

my heart heard itself being called

from the misty threshold of some dream.


To tell me its strange message,

that voice was coming from so far away

that more than a dream voice it seemed,

in its gray mystery, the shadow of an echo.


I was sitting at that instant

in a soft velvet armchair.

My arms rested on its arms

-how faint I felt them afterward!-

Then, crossing the glass panes

of a great balcony that faced the wide sky,

I saw a shadow enter. Perhaps the afternoon,

as it left, was coming in to see me... I believe so...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the suspended dream-threshold and the afternoon entering like a shadow.
